findings.title: V2 group-view lookup collects Resource UUIDs, not group IDs
findings.description:
Group resources are created with `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` (server-spi-private/.../AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121). That delegates to `create(server, null, name, owner)` (ResourceStore.java:45-46), and the JPA store assigns a random UUID as the ID (JPAResourceStore.java:65-66). So `getName()` is the group ID and `getId()` is a random UUID.

Line 122 passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission`, which calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (line 141). That lookup misses and falls back to the all-groups resource. Line 123 then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result. The V1 version at GroupPermissions.java:313-315 correctly uses `getName()`.

Impact:
- `UsersResource.getUsersCount` (lines 425, 430) passes this set to `getUsersCount(realm, …, groupIds)`. `JpaUserProvider` returns 0 for empty sets (lines 600-601, 683-684), so counts for group-scoped admins are 0.
- `UsersResource.searchForUser` (lines 448-451) skips setting `UserModel.GROUPS` when the set is empty. The DB then returns the first `max` users realm-wide, and the in-memory `canView` filter (line 460) drops most of them. Pages come back short or empty. The filter prevents over-exposure, so this is a correctness failure rather than a leak.
- `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest#testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` still passes, by my trace. The set is empty, so the group filter never applies, and the in-memory filter yields the expected single user. The test does not exercise the group filter.

Fix: use `groupResource.getName()` on lines 122-123. Add assertions on the user count and on paginated search for a group-scoped admin.

findings.title: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` lets VIEW-only grants create groups
findings.description:
`canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so a VIEW grant counts as manage. Its one real caller is `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (GroupsResource.java:181, `auth.groups().requireManage()`), which gates `POST /groups`. With an all-groups VIEW grant, which the test file already creates via `createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW))`, a view-only admin passes the check and can create top-level groups.

The interface javadoc at GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:73-76 documents this VIEW behavior, so the doc needs the same fix. `testManageAllGroups` only covers a caller with no permission and a MANAGE grant, so nothing catches this.

Fix: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`, correct the javadoc, and add a test that a VIEW-only all-groups caller gets 403 on `POST /groups`. VIEW belongs in `canView()` and `canList()`, not here.

findings.title: `/groups/count` is now reachable by view-only holders and returns unfiltered totals
findings.description:
V2 `canList()` is now `QUERY_GROUPS || canView()` (GroupPermissions.java:147-150), and V2 `canView()` includes VIEW and MANAGE grants (GroupPermissionsV2.java:46-53). Before this diff, V2 `canList()` was role-only, so view-only callers got 403 here.

`getGroupCount` calls `requireList()` and then returns `realm.getGroupsCount(...)` or `realm.getGroupsCountByNameContaining(search)` with no per-group filter. A caller with VIEW on one group can now read realm-wide totals and run name-prefix counts to enumerate group names they have no permission on.

Fix: apply the same per-group filter, or keep this endpoint behind a role check.

findings.title: Per-element V2 policy checks now run before pagination
findings.description:
The diff removed the `canViewGlobal` hoist here and in `GroupsResource.getGroups` (GroupsResource.java:113-114). Every subgroup now calls `auth.groups().canView(g)`. In V2 that means a role check, then `findByName`, possibly `findByResource` on the Groups all-resource, and a policy evaluation for each subgroup. `getSubGroups` applies the filter before `paginatedStream`, so the cost scales with the total subgroup count, not the page size. A caller with all-groups VIEW goes from one evaluation to N.

Fix: hoist the check again with `boolean all = auth.groups().canView();` and `filter(g -> all || auth.groups().canView(g))`. That is safe in V2. An all-groups grant also applies to a specific group resource, because DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:73-74 pulls in type-level policies.

findings.title: New V2 paths have no test coverage
findings.description:
Missing coverage:
1. A VIEW-only all-groups caller creating a group (FAIL 2).
2. User count and pagination with a group-scoped VIEW_MEMBERS grant (FAIL 1).
3. `/groups/count` for a view-only caller (CONCERN 3).

`testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` checks only the result size, which hides the broken group filter.

findings.title: `ADMIN` dropped from V2 `canView(user)` and `canManage(user)` without explanation
findings.description: `AdminRoles.ADMIN` is a realm role. RealmManager.java:346 creates it with `realm.addRole`, and it appears in `ALL_ROLES` but not `ALL_REALM_ROLES` (AdminRoles.java:30, 57). So `hasOneAdminRole(ADMIN, …)` was checking for a client role named "admin" on the admin client, which probably does not exist. Removing it is likely a no-op, but the change is not called out. Confirm the intent and mention it in the commit message.

findings.title: Existing realms won't get the new "Groups" all-resource
findings.description: `init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms set up before this change never get the "Groups" resource-type resource. `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` then passes `null` into `policyStore.findByResource` (GroupPermissionsV2.java:144-147), and the JPA policy lookup dereferences `resource.getId()` (JPAPolicyStore.java:215). The feature is EXPERIMENTAL (Profile.java:58), so the impact is limited. A null guard or a migration would close it.

findings.title: Removing the `canView` post-filter in `searchForUser` is safe
findings.description: The diff removed `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from `searchForUser`. Authorization is unchanged because `toRepresentation` applies the same filter (UsersResource.java:460). I checked this because the removal looked like a bypass.

findings.title: Two V2 evaluators use different resource-ID checks
findings.description: `UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission` only counts permissions whose `getResourceId()` matches the evaluated resource. `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` does not apply that check. I did not determine which behavior is correct, but the two should match or the difference should be documented.

findings.title: Shared test realm now grants `QUERY_GROUPS` to every fgap test
findings.description: `myadmin` is shared by the whole fgap package through `AbstractPermissionTest`. Adding `QUERY_GROUPS` changes the baseline for every test in that package. Confirm this is intended, or grant the role per test.

findings.title: Javadoc says `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` returns a Stream
findings.description: The `@return` tag says "Stream of IDs", but the method returns `Set<String>`. The doc also does not mention the empty-result cases for cross-realm admins and missing resource servers.
